title: The Deadline of the Green Zone
premise: Cyrus Okafor, a former aviation data analyst living under four names since exposing a covert rendition program, spots an anomaly no one else can see: a passenger flight erased from every radar and registry while still airborne. Pursued by an assassin who only knows her oldest alias, she races to deliver the flight's black-box evidence to a journalist inside a contested border zone, betting that the checkpoint's shift change is her only window. She gets the truth out at devastating personal cost—her final identity burned, her past made public—but forces three governments into an inquiry they can no longer bury, choosing a visible, dangerous life over safe anonymity.
about_author: Cyrus Zhou is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade writing risk assessments for companies he now refuses to name. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Living as 'Mara Voss' in a Rotterdam boarding house, Cyrus works nights scrubbing data to stay invisible—until her old monitoring scripts flag Flight 7714 vanishing mid-air from every system simultaneously. Recognizing the signature of the program she once exposed, she realizes someone is erasing people, not just records. Emotional beat: dread reawakening; the past she fled has found a new shape.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Mara
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and the assassin, 'Verhoeven'. A contact from her first life turns up dead, and Verhoeven—a fixer who has hunted her longest—narrows his search using her oldest alias. Cyrus decodes fragments of 7714's flight recorder smuggled out by a guilt-ridden air traffic controller, learning who was aboard: a witness three governments want gone. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, with interludes from the journalist Amara Diallo waiting in the Green Zone border compound. Cyrus crosses two countries with the recorder hidden in medical equipment, evading Verhoeven after a near-fatal encounter at a rail yard. She reaches the checkpoint as the shift change begins—but the borders have quietly closed, and the assassin is already inside the queue. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into cold clarity; she stops running.

chapters.title: What the Light Shows
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, closing with Diallo's broadcast. At the checkpoint, Cyrus chooses exposure over escape: she surrenders the recorder publicly, names herself on camera, and lets Verhoeven take her—knowing a vanished whistle-blower proves everything. The arrest goes viral before the assassin's handlers can contain it; the inquiry she once triggered from the shadows now ignites in daylight. Emotional beat: costly justice; belonging finally claimed through visibility rather than erasure.
